translationRepairs: In the thirtieth year, when Shizu entered the capital to attack the prime culprit, he was imprisoned in the Central Secretariat sub-bureau of the palace attendants' office; he was several times on the point of being killed, yet in the end came to no harm.

In the thirtieth year, when Shizu entered the capital to attack the prime culprit, he was imprisoned in the lower office of the Palace Attendants; he was several times on the point of being killed, yet in the end came to no harm.
侍中下省 is the lower office of the Palace Attendants; the source contains no Central Secretariat office here.

Grand Preceptor Liu Yigong, Prince of Jiangxia, stepped down as Director of the Masters of Writing and was named Supervisor of the Masters of Writing; General of Agile Cavalry Liu Yuanjing was appointed Director of the Masters of Writing.

Grand Preceptor Liu Yigong, Prince of Jiangxia, stepped down as Director of the Masters of Writing and was named Supervisor of the Central Secretariat; General of Agile Cavalry Liu Yuanjing was appointed Director of the Masters of Writing.
中書監 is Supervisor of the Central Secretariat and is distinct from the 尚書令 office relinquished in the same sentence.

Grand Preceptor the Prince of Jiangxia, Liu Yigong, was relieved of Director of the Masters of Writing and given the additional post of Supervisor of the Masters of Writing; General of Agile Cavalry Liu Yuanjing was given the additional post of Director of the Masters of Writing.

Grand Preceptor the Prince of Jiangxia, Liu Yigong, was relieved of Director of the Masters of Writing and given the additional post of Supervisor of the Central Secretariat; General of Agile Cavalry Liu Yuanjing was given the additional post of Director of the Masters of Writing.
The literal field repeats the same office error: 中書監 belongs to the Central Secretariat, not the Masters of Writing.
General of Agile Cavalry Liu Yuanjing was given the additional title of Grand Master with the Golden Ax and Ceremonies Equal to the Three Dukes.
General of Agile Cavalry Liu Yuanjing was granted the privilege of opening an office with ceremonies equal to the Three Dukes.
開府儀同三司 grants the privilege of opening an office with ceremonies equal to the Three Dukes; the source does not mention a golden ax.
On yichou day Liu Ziluan, Prince of Xin'an, General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Southern Xuzhou, was relieved of his concurrent post as Minister over the Masses.
On yichou day Liu Ziluan, Prince of Xin'an, General Who Comforts the Army and Inspector of Southern Xuzhou, was relieved of his concurrent post as Minister over the Masses.
撫軍將軍 is conventionally distinguished here as General Who Comforts the Army, rather than the 鎮軍 title.
On yichou day Liu Ziluan, Prince of Xin'an, General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Southern Xuzhou, was relieved of his concurrent post as Minister over the Masses.
On yichou day Liu Ziluan, Prince of Xin'an, General Who Comforts the Army and Inspector of Southern Xuzhou, was relieved of his concurrent post as Minister over the Masses.
The literal field likewise collapses 撫軍將軍 into a different military title; General Who Comforts the Army matches established Songshu usage.
On xinchou day in the ninth month, Liu Yu, Prince of Xiangdong, General Who Protects the Army, was made chief General Who Protects the Army.
On xinchou day in the ninth month, Liu Yu, Prince of Xiangdong, General Who Protects the Army, was made General Who Leads the Army.
The sentence explicitly changes Liu Yu from 護軍將軍 to 領軍將軍, so the latter cannot be a chief grade of the former.
On xinchou day in the ninth month, Liu Yu, Prince of Xiangdong, General Who Protects the Army, was made General Who Protects the Army in chief.
On xinchou day in the ninth month, Liu Yu, Prince of Xiangdong, General Who Protects the Army, was made General Who Leads the Army.
The literal field repeats the 護軍/領軍 collapse; General Who Leads the Army preserves the change of office.

On wuwu day Liu Yu, Prince of Xiangdong, was made General of the Guard and Inspector of Southern Yuzhou; Liu Xiuren, Prince of Jian'an, became chief General Who Protects the Army; Liu Xiuyou, Prince of Shanyang and Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, was appointed Inspector of Yuzhou; Liu Xiufan, Prince of Guiyang, became Central Army Guard; and Liu Zifang, Prince of Xunyang, was transferred from Southern Yuzhou to Eastern Yang Province.

On wuwu day Liu Yu, Prince of Xiangdong, was made General of the Guard and Inspector of Southern Yuzhou; Liu Xiuren, Prince of Jian'an, became General Who Leads the Army; Liu Xiuyou, Prince of Shanyang and Supervisor of the Palace Library, was appointed Inspector of Yuzhou; Liu Xiufan, Prince of Guiyang, became Central Army Guard; and Liu Zifang, Prince of Xunyang, was transferred from Southern Yuzhou to Eastern Yang Province.
The proposed repair correctly distinguishes 領軍將軍 from 護軍將軍 and identifies 祕書監 as Supervisor of the Palace Library.

On wuwu day Liu Yu, Prince of Xiangdong, General Who Protects the Army in chief, was made General of the Guard and Inspector of Southern Yuzhou; Liu Xiuren, Prince of Jian'an, General Who Protects the Army, was made General Who Protects the Army in chief; Liu Xiuyou, Prince of Shanyang, Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, was made Inspector of Yuzhou; Liu Xiufan, Prince of Guiyang, General of the Left Guard, was made Central Army Guard; Liu Zifang, Prince of Xunyang, Inspector of Southern Yuzhou, was made Inspector of Eastern Yang Province.

On wuwu day Liu Yu, Prince of Xiangdong, General Who Leads the Army, was made General of the Guard and Inspector of Southern Yuzhou; Liu Xiuren, Prince of Jian'an, General Who Protects the Army, was made General Who Leads the Army; Liu Xiuyou, Prince of Shanyang, Supervisor of the Palace Library, was made Inspector of Yuzhou; Liu Xiufan, Prince of Guiyang, General of the Left Guard, was made Central Army Guard; Liu Zifang, Prince of Xunyang, Inspector of Southern Yuzhou, was made Inspector of Eastern Yang Province.
The literal field contains both office errors; the proposal restores the distinct 領軍 and 護軍 titles and the Palace Library office.

Liu Xiuren, Prince of Jian'an, General Who Protects the Army in chief, was made General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yongzhou; Liu Yu, Prince of Xiangdong, General of the Guard, was restored as Inspector of Southern Yuzhou.

Liu Xiuren, Prince of Jian'an, General Who Leads the Army, was made General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yongzhou; Liu Yu, Prince of Xiangdong, General of the Guard, was restored as Inspector of Southern Yuzhou.
領軍將軍 is General Who Leads the Army, not a chief form of General Who Protects the Army.
I hold the three extremities and the winds are clear throughout the realm; with axe and lightning I have cut down the guilty, and at the hour of mao justice was done.
I hold the three extremities and the winds are clear throughout the realm; with axe and lightning I have cut down the guilty, and this latter-day arch-traitor has been put to death.
正卯 evokes Shaozheng Mao, the notorious minister executed by Confucius; it is not the earthly-branch hour mao. The revision makes the allusion intelligible in English.
I occupy the three extremities and the winds are clear throughout the myriad realms; with axe and lightning I cut off, and at the hour of mao the execution is carried out.
I occupy the three extremities and the winds are clear throughout the myriad realms; with the axe I make a lightning judgment, and this latter-day arch-traitor is hereby executed.
The literal field also mistakes 正卯 for a time of day. The revision retains the Shaozheng Mao allusion and the proclamation's syntax.

I mean to look up and proclaim the legacy of my forebears and look down to extend the bright fortune of the throne; night after night I dream of the cauldron in the kitchen, and when I think of the plank road I do not forget the hour before dawn.

I mean to look up and proclaim the legacy of my forebears and look down to extend the bright fortune of the throne; night after night I dream of the kitchen cauldron, and when I think of rammed-earth building I do not forget the hour before dawn.
板築 is rammed-earth construction and invokes Fu Yue's discovery at a building site; it is not a plank road.
Shen Qingzhi, Duke of Shixing, was appointed Grand Marshal; Wang Xuamo, General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Qing and Ji provinces, was made chief General Who Protects the Army.
Shen Qingzhi, Duke of Shixing, was appointed Grand Marshal; Wang Xuamo, General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Qing and Ji provinces, was made General Who Leads the Army.
領軍將軍 is again a distinct office and should be General Who Leads the Army, not chief General Who Protects the Army.
Shen Qingzhi, Duke of Shixing, was made Grand Marshal; Wang Xuamo, General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Qing and Ji provinces, was made General Who Protects the Army in chief.
Shen Qingzhi, Duke of Shixing, was made Grand Marshal; Wang Xuamo, General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Qing and Ji provinces, was made General Who Leads the Army.
The literal field repeats the same 領軍/護軍 confusion; the proposed office title is correct.
On xinchou day Liu Ziluan, Prince of Xin'an, General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Southern Xuzhou, was stripped of rank and ordered to take his own life.
On xinchou day Liu Ziluan, Prince of Xin'an, General Who Comforts the Army and Inspector of Southern Xuzhou, was stripped of rank and ordered to take his own life.
撫軍將軍 should remain General Who Comforts the Army, matching the same title in s0035 and established Songshu usage.

On dingwei day Liu Yu, Prince of Xiangdong, General of the Guard, was given the additional title of Grand Master with the Golden Ax and Ceremonies Equal to the Three Dukes; Liu Zunkao, Special Advance and Right Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, was made General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Southern Yuzhou; Yin Xiaozu, General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, was made Inspector of Yanzhou.

On dingwei day Liu Yu, Prince of Xiangdong, General of the Guard, was granted the privilege of opening an office with ceremonies equal to the Three Dukes; Liu Zunkao, Special Advance and Right Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, was made General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Southern Yuzhou; Yin Xiaozu, General Who Pacifies the North, was made Inspector of Yanzhou.
開府儀同三司 does not mention a golden ax, and established Songshu usage renders 寧朔將軍 as General Who Pacifies the North.
On xinhai day Liu Xiuyou, Prince of Shanyang, General of the Right and Inspector of Yuzhou, was promoted to General Who Pacifies the West.
On xinhai day Liu Xiuyou, Prince of Shanyang, General of the Right and Inspector of Yuzhou, was promoted to Grand General Who Stabilizes the West.
鎮西大將軍 is the grand-general form of the Stabilizes-the-West title, not 安西將軍, General Who Pacifies the West.

On yiyou day Liu Xiuyou, Prince of Shanyang, General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yuzhou, was made General Who Pacifies the Army and given the title of Grand Master with the Golden Ax and Ceremonies Equal to the Three Dukes.

On yiyou day Liu Xiuyou, Prince of Shanyang, Grand General Who Stabilizes the West and Inspector of Yuzhou, was made Grand General Who Stabilizes the Army and granted the privilege of opening an office with ceremonies equal to the Three Dukes.
The source has the grand-general titles 鎮西大將軍 and 鎮軍大將軍, followed by 開府儀同三司; the revision preserves all three distinctions without inventing a golden ax.
Shamans had said that the hall was haunted:"
Shamans had said that the hall was haunted.
The current idiomatic sentence ends with an unmatched quotation mark; the proposed punctuation yields a complete indirect statement.

To the Minister over the Masses, the chief General Who Protects the Army, and the Eight Dignitaries: Though Ziye was the eldest son of the proper wife, from childhood he showed a vicious and poisonous nature; his want of benevolence and filial piety was evident even in his earliest years.

To the Minister over the Masses, the concurrent General Who Protects the Army, and the Eight Dignitaries: Though Ziye was the eldest son of the proper wife, from childhood he showed a vicious and poisonous nature; his want of benevolence and filial piety was evident even in his earliest years.
領護軍 identifies the official concurrently holding the Protects-the-Army command, not a chief grade of that command.
From Yuan Kai downward, all were beaten and dragged about.
From the chief ministers downward, all were beaten and dragged about.
元凱 is the classical collective for worthy ministers, not a person named Yuan Kai.
From Yuan Kai downward, all were beaten and dragged about.
From the worthy ministers downward, all were beaten and dragged about.
The literal field also mistakes the collective 元凱 for a personal name; plain English better communicates the classical reference.
That he escaped destruction was also a piece of good fortune.
That he perished when he did was itself a mercy.
In this appraisal 得亡 means that his death itself was fortunate or merciful, as the idiomatic field already recognizes; it does not mean he escaped destruction.
